title: The Contribution of Paresis, Age and the Effect of a Short Training on Cognitive-Motor Dual Task Interference After Stroke: A Pilot Study
content:
Simultaneously performed cognitive and motor tasks after stroke interfered with each other. Considering the competing deficits of cognition and motor paresis we aim to assess overall functional impairments of patients after stroke injury. 
A range of dual-task (DT) assessments were made on 63 post-stroke patients (PS) and 49 healthy age-matched controls. Patients with paresis (P) and without paresis (NP) were compared with controls before and after DT training. 
Difference between the NP patients and controls confirmed the cognitive decline, while compared to the NP patients the motor damage was strengthened in P patients. Older cohort performed worse. According to the ArtAnova analysis, age was more important in DT performance than paresis. Short-term training modified the test results, especially in P patients. 
Paresis and higher age significantly worsen outcomes of the cognitive-dual task tests. Age-dependent results may reflect cognitive decline, especially in NP patients. Consequently, dual-task test results may represent global cognitive deterioration after stroke. Short-term dual task training improves dual task performances especially in the P groups.
Trial registration  https://www.isrctn.com/ISRCTN12362945 14/02/2023.
